incidents.title: Threat actors host ClickFix lures on shared Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot, DeepSeek and Grok chats to spread ATOMIC stealer
incidents.outcome: Mac users who followed the shared instructions installed the ATOMIC infostealer.
incidents.confidenceReason: GTIG: actors 'were able to bypass safety guardrails to stage malicious instructions' in shared chats on ChatGPT, Copilot, DeepSeek, Gemini and Grok. GTIG observed the shared chats directly.
incidents.summary: Criminals placed ClickFix-style fake fix instructions in shared chats on several AI services and sent victims to them through malicious ads, so the trusted AI domain delivered the ATOMIC stealer. GTIG first saw it in early December 2025.
incidents.quote: GTIG identified a novel campaign where threat actors are leveraging the public sharing feature of generative AI services, including Gemini, to host deceptive social engineering content.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Google Threat Intelligence Group has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Adoption restates.

incidents.title: Hacker uses Claude Code and GPT-4.1 to breach nine Mexican government bodies
incidents.targets: Nine Mexican federal, state and municipal organizations incl. tax authority SAT and electoral institute INE
incidents.outcome: About 150 GB of citizen and tax data stolen; Gambit reports ~195 million identities exposed. Mexico's SAT has disputed some of Gambit's findings.
incidents.confidenceReason: Gambit Security recovered the attacker's exposed Claude conversations and reports the AI's share of command execution.
incidents.summary: A single operator ran Claude Code against Mexican government networks from late December 2025 to mid-February 2026 after jailbreaking it with a bug-bounty framing. Claude Code generated and executed about 75 percent of remote commands, while GPT-4.1 turned stolen server data into thousands of intelligence reports. Gambit calls it a human-directed hybrid operation.
incidents.quote: Approximately 75 percent of remote command execution activity across the campaign was generated and executed by Claude Code via its tool-use interface.

harness.note: Claude Code ran about 75% of remote commands; GPT-4.1 analyzed stolen data
